provenance: [REVIEWED] research/v3/ORACLE_QUESTION_SET.md v2 §A.6, schema group group-a.probes.v1.1. Probe wordings and the derivation are committed there before any inference exists.
design_notes: v1.1, 2026-08-03: REFERENT FIX. The reviewer stress-tested v1 with an artwork that is half blue sky, half red tiled roof, with title text over both, and found a structural defect: v1 called the background "the large area", a SINGULAR referent, so on a plural background probes 2, 3, 5 and 6 read as unanswerable. v1.1 fixes the referent once, in a preamble carried byte-identically by every prompt file and by the human review form, and adds whole-region clauses to probes 2, 3, 5 and 6. The probe ids, the vocabulary and the derivation table are UNCHANGED — derivation.group-a.probes.v1.json is byte-identical, sha256 da67d5ebf0aaab0c593f8fb8e040192e0e688f9dccfcc9bb2fe6b2af391a2fc5.

Group-a.probes.v1 is the DECOMPOSED-PROBE ARM: six independently meaningful yes/no/unsure probes whose aggregate derives the tag, instead of one six-way question. Reviewer-initiated, 2026-08-03: "might increase reliability, and make the questions easier to answer." Full design: ORACLE_QUESTION_SET.md §A.6.
Every probe passes the five-second rule standing alone, and every probe is meaningful on its own terms — none of them is the six-way question in disguise.

`enclosure` is NOT decomposed. It is group A's most reliable field already (raw 0.87, kappa 0.60 inter-variant [MEASURED premise-run-1]); decomposing a reliable question spends decode for nothing. It is also held first in both bundled variants, both because that is the position the measured A->B ordering gain came from and because holding one field constant across arms makes it a control: if enclosure moves in this arm, something about the arm changed the model, not the question.
Derivation is a priori and committed: `derivation.group-a.probes.v1.json` enumerates all 3^6 = 729 answer vectors. An implementation that disagrees with any entry is wrong, not the table.

Variant Q asks the same six probes in a seeded random order (seed 20260803, the seed the oracle-validation fixtures use), recorded in `probe_order`. Ordering effects are measured-large in this question set (the A->B jump, ORACLE_QUESTION_SET.md design rule 6), so an arm claiming to be more reliable has to show that its probes are order-robust. P-vs-Q is that test.
Only the six probes are permuted. `enclosure` stays first and `shading_direction` stays last in both variants, so P-vs-Q isolates probe order and nothing else.
deviations: No `confidence` field and no `note` field, in either mode. Under group-a.v1 both were degenerate: 298 of 299 parsed rows said `high` and the same 298 left the note empty [MEASURED premise-run-1]. In this arm the per-probe `unsure` value IS the confidence, asked at the granularity where it can act, and the aggregate uncertainty instruments are the inconsistency and tension rates from the derivation table. Re-adding `note` to the bundled variants is a one-line change if the reviewer wants the audit trail back.

`shading_direction` is asked unconditionally, with `not_applicable` available, rather than conditionally on a prior `shaded_field` answer. The derivation forces `not_applicable` when the derived ground_type is not shaded_field. In group-a.v1 the radial_or_vignette<->not_applicable pair was 21 of 26 inter-variant disagreements on this field [MEASURED premise-run-1]; the arm removes that class by construction.

This arm asks no question whose answer is `ground_type`. `ground_type` and `field_texture` are DERIVED, by the committed table in `derivation.group-a.probes.v1.json`. Nothing downstream may re-derive them a second way.

No probe quotes the corrected criterion or the canonical examples from ORACLE_QUESTION_SET.md §A.2. That is the point of the arm: importing the hard construct into an "easy question" would make it the same question in more words. Where a canonical case bears on one probe it appears as a local clarification of that probe alone (`separate_areas`: "A blurry or soft join still counts as two areas").
referent_preamble: The background means everything behind the main subject and the text, taken AS A WHOLE — even if it has several different parts.
unsure_framing: Unsure is a real answer — some questions won't fit some artworks, and that is measured, not penalized.
system: You label album cover artwork for a research dataset. You answer only with the exact words offered. You never explain, never add fields, never use words that were not offered.
prompt:
Look at this album cover.

The background means everything behind the main subject and the text, taken AS A WHOLE — even if it has several different parts. Small details do not count. What the cover is about does not count. Whether it is attractive does not count.

Unsure is a real answer — some questions won't fit some artworks, and that is measured, not penalized.

Answer each question on its own. Do not try to make your answers tell one story.

1. enclosure - Is the artwork shut in by a border or a bar?
   thick_frame_or_bars - a wide frame, or a solid band along one or more edges, big enough to be an area in its own right
   none - the picture runs all the way out to the edges
   thin_border - a narrow keyline or thin frame

2. one_colour - Is the background essentially one single colour all over? If different parts have different colours, answer no.
   yes - one colour, all over
   no - more than one colour is present, or different parts have different colours
   unsure - you cannot tell

3. depicted_place - Taken as a whole, does the background show a place with depth — a room, a landscape, a street?
   yes - a place with depth is shown
   no - no place is shown
   unsure - you cannot tell

4. continuous_change - Does the background's colour change continuously — a fade, a glow, a vignette, colours melting into one another — across the whole background rather than only in one part of it? If it changes in one part and not in another, answer no.
   yes - it changes continuously, across the whole background
   no - it does not, or it only changes in one part
   unsure - you cannot tell

5. bg_visible - Can you make out a background at all — anything behind the main subject and the text?
   yes - there is a background you can see
   no - you cannot make out any background
   unsure - you cannot tell

6. motif_or_material - Is the background AS A WHOLE a repeating motif, or the surface of a material — paper, fabric, film grain, concrete, brush marks? If only one part of it is, answer no.
   yes - the whole background is a repeating motif, or a material surface
   no - neither, or only one part of it is
   unsure - you cannot tell

7. separate_areas - Can you point to two or more separate areas of the background, each with its own colour? A blurry or soft join still counts as two areas.
   yes - two or more separate areas, each its own colour
   no - you cannot pick out separate areas
   unsure - you cannot tell

8. shading_direction - If the background's colour changes across it, which way does it change?
   radial_or_vignette - spreading outward from a centre, or darkening into the corners
   not_applicable - the colour does not change across the background
   irregular - it changes, but with no simple geometry
   linear - it runs straight across, one edge to the other

Reply with JSON only.
